symbols.name: maxDuration
doc: Vercel stops a serverless function after a time limit. A question can legitimately take longer than the default (the language model may have to wait for its per-minute allowance), and an Executive Deep Synthesis makes two model calls and then a second reading of the best one (edsVerify.ts): with three circulars that is 30 s of writing and up to 30 s of checking. So I set 120 s here, and keep the engine's own deadline (EDS_DEADLINE_MS) under it.

symbols.name: ABSOLUTE_NOISE_FLOOR
doc: Google Gemini embeddings for completely unrelated text (e.g., Honda spark plugs) score about 0.55 - 0.62. Valid Hindi/cross-lingual or long conversational queries score about 0.68 - 0.78.

symbols.name: NAME_QUERY_VECTOR_BAR
doc: For a person-name-shaped query (2-3 pure-Latin words, e.g. "goutam debnath"), I require a circular or announcement to have a real textual anchor (the words appear) or an unusually strong vector match before it qualifies. Without this, off-topic documents ride the noise floor and surface as meaningless ~67% matches. I scoped it to name-shaped queries only, so cross-lingual semantic matches (which score ~0.68-0.78 with no shared words) are unaffected.

symbols.name: emptyBriefing
doc: I return a well-formed empty SynthesisResult so that intellectual-mode always gives the frontend the typed object it expects, never a bare string.

symbols.name: SYNTH_CHARS_PER_CIRCULAR
doc: This is how much text of each source circular I hand to the synthesis model. The UI snippet stays short (pickReadableExcerpt), but the synthesis needs the FULL circular, so that figures living in a different chunk than the one that matched the query (e.g. an OCR rate table, multi-page bond schedules or annexures) are fully in context. The model is Gemini Pro with a 2M token context window.

symbols.name: fetchFullCircularText
symbols.sig: async function fetchFullCircularText( dataSource: import("typeorm").DataSource, ids: number[],): Promise<Map<number, string>>
doc: Here I fetch the complete chunk text of the given circulars (all chunks, in order) and return a map id -> concatenated text. This is what feeds the synthesis, whichever single chunk matched the query vector.

symbols.name: pickReadableExcerpt
symbols.sig: function pickReadableExcerpt( chunkText: string | null | undefined, tokens: string[],): string
doc: The content engine may concatenate several chunks of a document with "\n\n". When the top-scoring chunk is OCR garbage (dense tables read as noise), I would rather SHOW the user a readable passage that still contains their words. I use this only to pick the best candidate chunk for DISPLAY. It never affects ranking or which documents match, and it must not.

symbols.name: shaped
symbols.sig: async function shaped(res: Response, signedIn: boolean): Promise<Response>
doc: Every search goes through here. This is PASSIVE route logging (step 2 of the front-path plan, src/lib/search/frontPathTrace.ts): the answer is exactly what handleSearch returns. I only add x-omni-* / Server-Timing headers and ONE console line saying which route answered, how long each stage took and how many model calls and tokens it used. I made sure tracing can never break a search. Here I shape the answer as it leaves: the ticket number and the P.No. masked for everybody (src/lib/security/sensitiveFields.ts), the SQL the model wrote kept on the server (answerSql.ts), and, only while VISITOR_CUT_ENABLED is on, a visitor's cut-down view.
